title: Attention Superposition in GPT-2: Quantifying Cross-Layer Attention Representations Using Probing

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if attention computations are highly entangled across layers, single-layer circuit analysis is unreliable for safety-critical applications. However, the step from 'quantifying entanglement' to 'improving safety monitoring' requires additional work not specified in the proposal.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires extracting Q/K/V vectors across all attention heads and a large token corpus, training pairwise linear probes for head-j from head-i outputs across layers. The combinatorial number of probes and the conceptual understanding of attention superposition is advanced for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The number of head pairs to probe grows quadratically with depth. A large corpus is needed for reliable probing. Multiple analysis dimensions (probe accuracy vs layer gap, fraction of entangled heads). This is sustained effort requiring multiple workstreams.

novelty.reasoning: Superposition and cross-layer entanglement are well-studied concepts (Anthropic's toy models, SAE work), and cross-layer probing has been explored in various forms. However, the specific approach of systematically training pairwise linear probes between all attention head Q/K/V outputs across layers to quantify the degree of cross-layer attention entanglement has not been directly published. Related work exists on layer-wise feature entanglement (e.g., features expanding and entangling with depth) but the specific probe-based quantification methodology for attention heads is a partial contribution.
